name: Acetylated distarch adipate
description: Acetylated distarch adipate (CAS 63798-35-6 ), also identified as E1422 , is a chemically modified starch produced by dual treatment with acetic anhydride and adipic anhydride. This dual modification delivers superior freeze-thaw stability and resistance to retrogradation compared to native starches, making it a reliable thickener and stabilizer across demanding food processing environments. In processed foods, E1422 maintains consistent texture and viscosity in sauces, dressings, soups, and fruit pie fillings that undergo freeze-thaw cycles or high-temperature processing. Dairy applications such as yogurts, cream-based desserts, and processed cheese benefit from its emulsification and water-binding capacity, which prevents syneresis and phase separation during shelf life. In the paper and pulp industry, it functions as a surface sizing and coating agent, improving paper strength and printability. Textile manufacturers apply it as a warp sizing agent to reduce yarn breakage. Acetylated distarch adipate is supplied as a white to off-white powder in food-grade and technical grades. The food-grade specification conforms to FCC and E1422 regulatory standards. Defined substitution levels govern the acetyl and adipate content within the chemical structure.
